expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: a confirm modal is the weakest device on the ladder for this

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: Users learn to reflex-click through 'Are you sure?' dialogs (that's the click-through blindness that's presumably how they're deleting workspaces)

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: soft-delete into a trash with a retention window (e.g. 30 days)

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: a 'Deleted. Undo' toast... No friction on the happy path, full recovery on the accidental one

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: If you still want a gate on top for the permanent purge... type-the-workspace-name-to-confirm

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: mentions type-the-workspace-name-to-confirm but does not require showing scope/scale of deletion

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: marks soft-delete + undo as 'the stronger fix', positions type-to-confirm as secondary for permanent purge only
